vision_features.image_context: Close-up of a soybean plant stem section showing multiple nodes with attached seed pods. The image focuses on the central stem and lateral branches bearing pods. The surrounding field background shows dry, brown, senescent plant material and exposed dark soil. Leaves are almost entirely absent from the visible stem sections.
vision_features.abnormalities:
1. Pods: The pods clustered at each node along the stem are notably small, flat, and thin — most appearing poorly filled or entirely empty (no visible seed bulging within the pod walls). They are tan to light golden-brown in color, elongated-oval in shape, approximately 15–25 mm in length. The pods have a dry, papery texture. There is no distinct border coloring; the surface is uniformly pale tan. Several pods appear shriveled or deflated rather than plump and rounded as would be expected at maturity.
2. Stem: The main stems remain green and appear relatively healthy in color (bright green), though they are notably slender. At the nodes, there are small dark specks or spots visible (approximately 1–2 mm, pinpoint to small in size), appearing as dark brownish-black dots on the node tissue and pod attachment points.
3. Surrounding plant material: The background plants and fallen leaves are completely dry, brown, and desiccated, indicating advanced or premature senescence across the field. The foliage on the focal plant is almost entirely absent.
vision_features.absences: 1. No plump, well-filled pods with visible seed outlines are present — the pods lack the rounded, bulging profile expected at full maturity. 2. No green leaf tissue is visible on the focal stem, which would normally still be present at early reproductive stages. 3. No powdery, fuzzy, or thread-like surface growth is visible on the pods or stems. 4. No large discolored marks or spreading stained areas are visible on the pod surfaces beyond the general uniform tan coloration.
vision_features.summary: The image shows a soybean stem at an advanced stage bearing multiple clusters of pods that appear uniformly small, flat, and poorly filled, with a dry, papery tan appearance. The surrounding field material is fully senescent and brown. The most striking feature is the near-complete absence of seed development within the pods — they appear deflated and empty rather than plump. The stems remain green, creating a stark contrast with the desiccated pods and background vegetation. The pods are the most severely affected organ, with their failure to fill being the single most unusual visual feature.

Knowledge-base entry for 'Diaporthe':
────────────────────────────────────────
For stem canker, initial symptoms are small, reddish-brown lesions near the nodes in the lower third of the canopy that expand into sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins; for pod and stem blight, the most characteristic sign is linear rows of black specks on mature soybean stems.. Mature plants with stem canker can exhibit irregular, thin black lines or 'zone' lines on the interior of lower stems; black specks (pycnidia) appear in linear rows on stems for pod and stem blight.. Knowledge-base entry for 'Phomopsis':
────────────────────────────────────────
Phomopsis-infected seeds are cracked and shriveled and often covered with chalky, white mold. Infected seedlings have reddish-brown, pinpoint lesions on the cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.. Seeds are cracked and shriveled with chalky white mold covering; seedlings show reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on stem near soil line.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Bacterial_Blight':
────────────────────────────────────────
Small, angular, reddish-brown lesions surrounded by a yellow halo; as disease progresses, lesions often grow together to produce large, irregularly shaped dead areas.. Centers of older lesions frequently fall out, causing leaves to appear tattered; symptoms usually begin in the upper canopy on young leaves.. Septoria brown spot, Bacterial pustule, Downy mildew, Soybean rust, Soybean vein necrosis, Insect and mite Injury
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Early symptoms include seed rot and damping off; the most characteristic symptom is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, which can girdle the stem causing stunting or death.. A dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, reaching as high as several nodes, girdling the stem; as disease progresses, damping off, stunting, yellowing, and brown lesions on lower stem can occur..
